predecessors.name: Duchy of Saxe-Weimar
predecessors.text: Saxe-Weimar and Saxe-Eisenach, united in the person of the duke since 1741 and formally merged on 20 September 1809

successors.name: German Empire
successors.text: the grand duchy as a constituent state of the German Empire from 1871

ledger.x: 1806: the duchies of Saxe-Weimar and Saxe-Eisenach, one duke since 1741, enter the Confederation of the Rhine.
4 August 1807: Napoleon takes Blankenhain from Saxe-Weimar.
20 September 1809: Weimar and Eisenach are merged into the Duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach.
1815: the Congress of Vienna raises the duchy to a grand duchy.
1815: the Neustadt district comes to Weimar.
1815: the Eisenacher Oberland is added in the west.
September 1815: Blankenhain and southern and eastern Erfurt lands pass from Prussia to Weimar.
1871: the grand duchy joins the German Empire as a constituent state.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussia won; Hesse-Kassel was incorporated into Prussia's Province of Hesse-Nassau and the grand duchy joined the North German Confederation.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary; the Napoleonic-era lands include exclaves (Blankenhain lost 1807, the Ilmenau, Allstedt, Oldisleben and Ostheim exclaves).
Treaty borders of the Vienna settlement of 1815; the exclaves of Ilmenau, Allstedt, Oldisleben and Ostheim stay as small enclaves.
